stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:

  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt

many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

{
 "path": ".openclaw/task-notes/task-4e0e0429.md",
 "content": "# Continual-ARC task family note: task-4e0e0429

## Inferred transformation (high confidence from five demos)
Inputs contain two equal-sized grids separated by a full row/column of a third, uniform separator color. Split the two panels at that separator and compare corresponding cells. Find the color shared by both panels (the demonstrated cases have a clear single shared color, often one panel's background and the other's foreground/background). Make an output the size of one panel, filled with that shared color. At coordinates where BOTH panels contain that shared color, put color 3 instead. Do not copy unrelated marks from either panel.

Evidence from demos:
- Demo 3: panels 2x10; shared color 8. Output is 8 everywhere except 3 where both aligned cells are 8.
- Demo 2: panels 9x27; shared color 9. Output uses 9 background and 3 exactly on coincident 9s.
- Demo 4: panels 30x11; shared color 1. Output uses 1 background and 3 on aligned 1/1 cells.
- Demo 5: panels 9x8; shared color 4. Output uses 4 background and 3 on aligned 4/4 cells.
- Demo 1: panels 14x14; shared color 8. Output all 8 because the lone 8 in panel 1 does not align with an 8 in panel 2.

## Critical implementation detail
Compare panel cells at identical row/column indices, not raw input columns. A vertical separator means take columns to its left/right; a horizontal separator means take rows above/below. Output color 3 only for (shared-color, shared-color) matches; otherwise use the shared color.

## Caution from this instance
The test was 26x21 with a vertical all-0 separator at column 10. Panels are 26x10: left columns 0-9 (colors 2/7), right columns 11-20 (colors 7/9). Their shared color is 7. Thus correct output should be 26x10, initialized to 7 and mark 3 wherever left[r][c] == 7 AND right[r][c] == 7. This agent submitted repeatedly incorrect grids due to manual coordinate transcription; compute the intersections programmatically or carefully row-by-row next time. The transformation concept is much more reliable than those submitted grids.
